SMEs guide

An insurance checklist for Kenyan small businesses

Chestnut Insurance Agency editorial team · Published 21 November 2026

Start with what you could not afford to lose: your premises and stock, your employees’ welfare, your customers’ claims against you, and your ability to keep trading. Then match each exposure to a cover and confirm the sums insured.

Step 1. List what you own and owe

  • Buildings, if you own them, and your lease obligations if you rent
  • Stock, equipment, furniture and fittings with replacement values
  • Vehicles and goods in transit
  • Cash handled and where it is kept

Step 2. List who you are responsible for

  • Employees, including casual and seasonal workers, for work injury cover
  • Customers and visitors on your premises
  • Clients who rely on your advice, if you provide professional services

Step 3. Match covers to risks

  • Fire and allied perils, burglary
  • Public liability
  • WIBA and, where suitable, group medical or life
  • Goods in transit or marine cargo
  • Professional indemnity or cyber, where relevant

Step 4. Prepare for a quotation

  • Asset list with realistic values
  • Payroll summary
  • Details of existing policies and renewal dates
  • Claims record for recent years

Step 5. Ask the right questions

  • What is excluded?
  • What is the excess?
  • Are there security or maintenance conditions?
  • What happens if my values are too low?

This guide is general education about insurance in Kenya. It is not legal or financial advice and does not describe any specific policy. Policy wording, exclusions and the law that applies at the time govern. Speak to an advisor about your situation.
